intro.title: Form Library from Scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form library from scratch in Angular to understand how form controls and validation work under the hood. You'll learn the core concept of reactive programming by creating a FormControl class that manages state and updates. The main technologies involved are TypeScript for type safety and Angular's dependency injection and change detection. You'll implement basic features like setting values, tracking validity, and handling user input changes. By the end, you'll have a foundational custom form control that you can extend with more advanced features.
intro.usecase: Building custom form libraries is essential for enterprise applications where standard form solutions don't meet complex validation, accessibility, or design system requirements. Developers implement these patterns in customer relationship management (CRM) systems, financial dashboards, and healthcare portals that need consistent form behavior across hundreds of input fields. For example, a banking application's loan approval form requires custom validation logic, real-time field dependencies, and specialized error messaging that off-the-shelf libraries can't provide. Creating your own form library gives teams complete control over form state management, validation rules, and integration with backend APIs while maintaining consistent user experience across the entire application.
